info.title: Invinite API
info.description:
Invinite financial data API. Each endpoint has a base credit cost: `x-credits` is the base cost; responses add 1 credit per started 1,000 rows beyond the first 1,000; `X-Credits-Charged` reports the final debit and `X-Credits-Included-Remaining` what is left of the plan's included credits. `GET /v1/account/usage` returns your account's usage by day, endpoint family and key (it costs no credits). SEC filing search has a 100-credit base cost.

**Coverage.** Financial data covers SEC registrants and US listings; a foreign suffix (`SAP.DE`, `VOD.L`) or a crypto pair (`X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404. A known company with no data in a family (for example no statements yet) answers 404 with `code: not_covered`; an empty page of a covered company stays 200 with an empty list. `GET /v1/company/available-companies` lists every known company.

## Webhooks

Accounts on LITE and above subscribe with `POST /v1/earnings-calls/webhooks` to the `earnings_call.*` lifecycle events (filtered by CIK) and, on STANDARD and above, to `news.published` (one delivery per new news item, filtered by the CIKs it mentions); see `x-webhooks` for each `data` object. What a subscription may hold depends on the plan (a create / update beyond it is refused with the plan's limit; `ping` needs no subscription — the test route and the disabled notice send it to any subscription):

| Plan | Webhooks | Events | CIKs per webhook | Keywords per webhook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FREE | 0 | — | — | — |
| LITE | 5 | `.scheduled`, `.rescheduled`, `.started`, `.ended`, `.transcript_ready`, `.assets_ready` | ≤ 10 | — |
| STANDARD | 15 | LITE + `.transcript_provisional`, `.transcript_corrected`, `.documents_updated`, `news.published` | ≤ 25 | — |
| PRO / ENTERPRISE | 50 | STANDARD + `.guidance_flash`, `.keyword_hit` | ≤ 100 | ≤ 20 (on ≤ 10 webhooks) |

Every delivery is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Invinite-Event`, `X-Invinite-Delivery` and `X-Invinite-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where `v1` = HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<t>.<raw body>`); during a secret rotation the header carries one `v1` per valid secret. Reject a signature older than 5 minutes. Any 2xx within 10 s acknowledges; redirects are not followed. A failed delivery is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h (8 attempts in all, the same delivery id each time). A subscription is disabled after 8 consecutive dead-lettered deliveries (a final `ping` with `notice: subscription_disabled` is sent). Deliveries are at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on the delivery id, order by `created_at`.

## Licensing

| Tier | display | redistribute | rag | train | audio | resell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FREE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| LITE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| STANDARD | ✓ | – | ✓ | – | – | – |
| PRO | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ | – |

Invinite data may be shown and, from PRO, redistributed inside the licensee's own product with attribution ("Source: Invinite" on screen or in the API response that carries it). It may never be resold, relicensed, white-labelled or offered as a data feed as the licensee's own data, at any tier, under any contract.

Policy version: 2026-10-draft. Draft — pending counsel sign-off.

Audio files carry a forensic watermark that identifies the recording. Audio is subject to per-company takedown and may not be re-hosted.

SEC data: Figures and filings originate from SEC EDGAR; the standardisation, mapping and derived metrics are Invinite's.

News: News text is Invinite's own summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication (the publisher's text and media are never served); the licensee shows the attribution (publisher, source URL and date) next to it; the resale rule applies.

PDF documents: Branded PDFs of transcripts and news items are permanent URLs to one shared file per version. They may be shown, downloaded and forwarded unmodified with the notice page intact; the resale rule applies unchanged. News PDFs carry Invinite's summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication under the attribution stated on their notice page; a PDF disappears when the item is taken down or its source's reuse is denied.

Every `/v1/*` data operation carries `x-license`, the minimum use right its data ships with; `GET /status/licensing` serves the same matrix per route, rendered at [data.invinite.com/docs/licensing](https://data.invinite.com/docs/licensing). `/v1/account/usage` serves no licensed data and carries none.

## Status

[`/status`](/status) reports whether each product family works (a status and its uptime over 7, 30 and 90 days); [`/status/licensing`](/status/licensing) serves the licensing matrix per route. The status routes need no API key and are cached for 5 minutes. The public status page is [status.data.invinite.com](https://status.data.invinite.com): a snapshot of `/status` every 15 minutes plus an external reachability probe of the API.

Uptime is the share of requests answered without a server error, measured by the API per product family; a window with too little traffic to judge shows no figure. Status reflects the last 24 hours.

Product families: Company, Financials, SEC Filings, Insider Trades, Institutional Ownership, IPOs, Market, Metadata, Earnings Calls, News, WebSocket, Account.

WebSocketSubscribeEarningsCall.description: Client frame: subscribe to the live transcript of one earnings call, by event_id or by cik (the call that is live or starts within ±2 h), or with scope: all_live (no event_id / cik) to every call being captured live — keyword hits only, never segments, one subscription slot. Requires the PRO plan.

event_id.description: Event id from the earnings-calls REST routes

scope.description: all_live = every live call (keywords required, error keywords_required without); then no event_id / cik

since_seq.description: Last final seq the client holds; finals after it are replayed before live delivery (-1 = from the first final)

partials.description: Also receive partial (not yet final) segments

prices.description: Also receive price_tick frames of the call's stock (≤ 1 per second while the call is live). Per-call only: with scope: all_live the subscribe is refused (bad_message). GET /v1/earnings-calls/live says live_prices: true when ticks flow

keywords.description: Keyword alerts: a keyword_hit frame for every FINAL segment that contains one (whole words, case-insensitive, multi-word allowed). Held for this subscription only

keyword_match.description: exact = whole-word match of your spelling (buyback never matches buybacks); stem = also s / es / ed / ing / 's per word (tariff matches tariffs)

speaker_roles.description: Only hits spoken by one of these roles (from the provisional live speaker names; a hit whose speaker is still unnamed passes)

min_rank.description: all_live only: calls of companies ranked ≤ min_rank by market cap

events.description: all_live only: what reaches the subscription (default keyword_hit; add guidance_flash to receive the flashes of every live call)

WebSocketSubscribedEvent.description: A subscription is active. A per-call subscription carries the call (event_id … state); a scope: all_live subscription carries scope, keywords and live_calls instead

current_seq.description: Highest final seq seen so far; null before the first final (seqs start at 0)

keywords.description: all_live only: the keywords as held

live_calls.description: all_live only: calls being captured live that the subscription follows right now

WebSocketKeywordHitEvent.description: A subscribed keyword occurred in a FINAL segment (layer live; partials are never evaluated) or, once per subscription at transcript_ready, in the final transcript (layer final; a final hit within ± 5 s of a live hit of the same keyword is not repeated). The only call-level frame of a scope: all_live subscription besides guidance_flash

keyword.description: The subscriber's own spelling of the keyword

seq.description: The live final's seq; null on the final layer

start_ms.description: live: milliseconds from call_t0; final: offset from the start of the recording

end_ms.description: null on the final layer when the cleaned text has no end timing

text.description: The segment (live) or turn (final), at most 500 chars

context_before.description: The previous final / turn of the call (≤ 300 chars); a final is often half a sentence

speaker_name.description: From the live speaker-name snapshot (null while unnamed) or the final transcript

speaker_role.description: executive | ir_host | analyst | operator; null while unnamed

layer.description: live = a live final; final = the final transcript at transcript_ready (once per subscription)

latency_ms.description: live only: relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time, so it includes the transcript's release hold of about 8 s (excludes the client's network); null when the call's clock is unknown

WebSocketGuidanceFlashEvent.description: A forward-looking guidance number extracted from the live transcript seconds after it was spoken (one frame per metric / period; a restatement repeats it with a higher revision). Sent to every subscription of the call and to all_live subscriptions whose events include guidance_flash. Provisional: the structured guidance of /v1/earnings-calls/extractions replaces it after the call

seq.description: The final that triggered the extraction

revision.description: 1 for the first flash of a metric / period; higher when the numbers were restated

low.description: Lower bound of the range (absolute units)

point.description: A point value when no range was given

currency.description: ISO 4217 when a currency applies

source_sentence.description: The verbatim sentence the numbers come from

start_ms.description: Milliseconds of the sentence from call_t0

WebSocketPriceTickEvent.description: One second of the call's stock price while the call is live (≤ 1 per second, only seconds with a trade — hold the last value and draw a missing second as a gap; pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse). Sent only to per-call subscriptions with prices: true. Temporal coincidence, not attribution of cause. The minute rows of /v1/earnings-calls/price-attribution are the backlog for a late join

at.description: Start of the one-second bar (ISO 8601 UTC)

call_ms.description: The bar start on the transcript clock (the start_ms of transcript_segment frames); null before the call's clock is known — then chart it on wall time (at)

price.description: Last price of the second, shown while the call is live

cumulative_volume.description: Shares traded so far today; null when unknown

reference_price.description: The call's reference: the last trade before the call start (for a late join, the previous close)

return_bps.description: Return since reference_price, basis points; null without a reference

day_return_bps.description: Return since prev_close, basis points; null without it

source.description: stream = the real-time per-second bar; snapshot = the polled last trade while the stream is down (open = high = low = price)

WebSocketWarningEvent.description: A subscription is degraded but keeps running: global_scope_degraded = a new live call was not attached because this server already follows its cap of live calls (sent once per subscription while the cap holds)

WebSocketTranscriptSegmentEvent.description: One live transcript segment. seq is strictly increasing per call but not contiguous; a partial carries the seq its final will get. Finals and partials are released about 8 s after recognition, a quality hold (https://data.invinite.com/docs/live-sync)

start_ms.description: Milliseconds from call_t0 (GET /v1/earnings-calls/live/stream), the audio's clock

WebSocketSpeakerNamesEvent.description: Provisional live speaker names (the newest snapshot; the final transcript's naming replaces them). A final's name = the assignment of its speaker_label whose seq range covers its seq

WebSocketCallLifecycleEvent.description: A phase of the call: call_started, call_ended, transcript_provisional, transcript_ready or rescheduled. transcript_ready and rescheduled end the subscription (an unsubscribed frame follows; after rescheduled, subscribe again with the same event_id)

live_transcript_available.description: call_ended only: the provisional live transcript is available (null = unknown)

WebSocketGapEvent.description: No final between after_seq and next_seq arrived within the reorder wait (a capture relaunch skips 1,000+ numbers with nothing lost, or finals were never published). A late final may still follow: order by seq

WebSocketUnsubscribedEvent.description: A subscription ended: on request, after transcript_ready / rescheduled, 2 h after call_ended without transcript_ready, when the call will produce nothing more (capture failed, no call, published), or 12 h after the scheduled start

reason.description: requested | transcript_ready | rescheduled | no_transcript (2 h after call_ended) | call_not_live (capture failed, no call, or published) | max_duration (12 h after the scheduled start)

WebSocketErrorEvent.description: A client frame was refused (unavailable = an unexpected server failure, retry shortly); the socket stays open

channel.description: news.live for a refusal of a news frame (channel_unavailable = live news is switched off; read GET /v1/news)

get.description:
The SEC-sourced IPO calendar: one row per registration statement of a company that is not listed yet, from its first public S-1 or F-1 until it trades or is withdrawn, keyed by CIK. Each row carries the stage, the proposed ticker(s), the price range and final price from the prospectus, the SEC timestamps of every step, and the filings that moved it.

`GET /v1/ipos` is a different source: the Massive IPO calendar, keyed by ticker, whose rows usually appear only near pricing. A registration shows up weeks earlier. `massive` holds the Massive row matched to a registration (by ticker and issuer name), `proposed_symbols[].ipo_calendar_match` flags a proposed ticker that is on that calendar, and each `GET /v1/ipos` row links back through `registration`.

`ipo_pending` carries the issuer lifecycle's IPO-pending entry of the same track (proposed symbols, profile, logo); `pending=true` lists only tracks with an open one. Issuers that are IPO-pending without an S-1 / F-1 registration track are on `GET /v1/sec/issuers?phase=public_preipo`.

Pre-IPO companies have no ticker yet: read their filings with `GET /v1/sec/filings?identifier=<cik>`.

Minimum tier for redistribute: PRO.

Upcoming and past earnings calls of all covered US companies in a window of days (default today + 14 days, at most 92). Each day is a calendar day in New York time (America/New_York); a call without a confirmed time is listed on its announced date. `event_type=all` returns every event type.

Each event carries `calendar` (appended 2026-11): the results release (`report`: day, BMO / AMC from the results filing's acceptance, the filing) and the call (`call`: status, day, time and how good it is, the stating source) kept apart, the event `status` (reported, confirmed, announced, estimated, postponed, cancelled) beside `date_status`, and coverage `warnings`. `date_kind=report` selects the window on the report day; `calendar_status` filters on `calendar.status`.

Expired rows (`capture_status` `expired`: an estimate that never became a call, a duplicate, a non-call issuer; `expired_reason` says which) are a final status and omitted unless `include_expired=true` (appended 2026-11).

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

Minimum tier for display: FREE.

get.description:
A temporary HLS playlist URL of an earnings call's live audio (PRO). The stream is watermarked.

### Using the URL

- The URL works until `expires_at` (2 hours by default) and is minted fresh on every request: request a new one before it expires.

- Play it with hls.js, Safari or VLC. The playlist is an EVENT playlist, so seek to 0 for the start of the call.

- `call_t0` is the wall clock of call ms 0: `#EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME` minus `call_t0` = the `start_ms` of the live transcript (WebSocket channel `live_channel`).

- The audio is released as live as possible, a few seconds behind our capture. Transcript segments are released about 8 s after recognition, a quality hold, so the text trails the audio: [Live audio and transcript sync](https://data.invinite.com/docs/live-sync) has the timing and how to play both in sync.

### No stream and errors

- `status` `not_started` / `disabled` answer `url: null`.

- `403 audio_unavailable` when the company's audio is not licensed for delivery.

- `503 media_unavailable` while live streaming is not configured.

### Choose the call

- By `event_id`, or

- by `identifier` with `year` + `quarter` (fiscal), or

- by `identifier` with `date` (a calendar day in New York time (America/New_York); a call without a confirmed time is listed on its announced date). With `date`, `event_type` (default `earnings_call`) also addresses an investor day, conference or shareholder meeting.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served; a foreign suffix (`SAP.DE`, `VOD.L`) or a crypto pair (`X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404.

Minimum tier for display: FREE.

Forward guidance or every reported KPI figure of one earnings call.

- `kind=guidance`: one consolidated item per metric, period and basis, with verbatim citations.

- `kind=kpi`: every reported KPI figure.

- Guidance items are cross-validated between the call and the press release; `cross_validated=false` items come from one source only.

- `confidence` is calibrated on large-cap spot checks, not a probability.

- `filing_link` points at the SEC filing that carries the same figure: the results 8-K's press release (`target=press_release`, matched on the text) or, once the 10-Q / 10-K is on EDGAR, its XBRL fact (`target=periodic_filing`, `concept`), which replaces the 8-K link.

- `match_kind=rounded` means the filing's value rounds to the figure as spoken.

### Paging

- A page can hold fewer than `limit` items while `next_url` is still set: items (and KPI mentions) that only a press release no longer served supports are dropped after paging.

- `metric` is matched against the normalized vocabulary: `revenue`, `eps_gaap`, `eps_non_gaap`, `operating_margin`, `operating_income`, `gross_margin`, `opex`, `capex`, `fcf`, `tax_rate`, `share_count`, `ebitda`, `net_income`, `revenue_growth`, `eps_gaap_growth`, `eps_non_gaap_growth`, `operating_income_growth`, `ebitda_growth`, `net_income_growth`, `fcf_growth`, `opex_growth`, `capex_growth`, `ebitda_margin`, `fcf_margin`, `fcf_conversion`, `opex_pct_revenue`, `capex_pct_revenue`, `other`, plus dynamic `segment:<slug>` (a segment's revenue) and `segment_growth:<slug>` metrics.

- Amount metrics (`revenue`, `eps_gaap`, `eps_non_gaap`, `operating_income`, `opex`, `capex`, `fcf`, `ebitda`, `net_income`, `share_count`, `segment:<slug>`) never carry `unit=pct`: a growth rate or a share of revenue is its own metric (`revenue_growth`, `ebitda_margin`, `capex_pct_revenue`, `fcf_conversion` …), always in `pct`. Growth rates are signed (a decline is negative).

- An unknown metric returns an empty series.

### How far to trust it

- Guidance items are cross-validated between the call and the press release; `cross_validated=false` items come from one source only.

- `confidence` is calibrated on large-cap spot checks, not a probability.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served; a foreign suffix (`SAP.DE`, `VOD.L`) or a crypto pair (`X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404.

Minimum tier for redistribute: PRO.

A company's investor-relations documents, newest year first: annual reports, proxy statements, ESG / governance documents, investor-day and conference decks, shareholder letters, fact sheets, and link-only webcast replay pages. By default the IR library outside its earnings calls' folders; `include=calls` adds the documents of every earnings call (CFO commentary, data sheets, letters, the company's own transcript, prepared remarks, 10-Q / 10-K links) to the same list, marked `source: call` with the call's `event_id`, so one paged list holds the company's whole document tree.

Filter by IR section, kind, year, period or event, or by the document tree: `category`, `group` (a folder and everything below it) and `fiscal_year` / `fiscal_quarter` (the earnings folder `earnings/fy<YYYY>/q<N>`). On a call document `year` / `period` are the call's fiscal year / quarter; a `section` filter matches IR-library rows only. Documents of one earnings call alone are on `/v1/earnings-calls/documents`; a call's press release and slide deck are on `/v1/earnings-calls/press-release` and `/v1/earnings-calls/slides`. A press release that is no call or event material is a news item: `GET /v1/news?publisher=320193`.

### Order and paging

- Without `include`: newest year first, then IR section, kind and title. With `include=calls`: newest year first, then folder (`group`), kind, title and id, one total order over both sources, so `offset` pages never skip or repeat a document.

### The document tree

Every stored document sits in one folder of the company's document tree: `group` (its path) under one of eight `category` spine folders, in this order: `earnings` (`earnings/fy2027/q2` = one fiscal quarter's call: release, deck, CFO commentary, data sheets, transcript; `earnings/cy2026/08-26` = a call without a fiscal period), `events` (`events/2026/09-10-<event>` = a conference, investor day or shareholder meeting; its `group_label` reads the event's date and name, e.g. "May 18, 2025 · GTC Taipei 2025"), `reports` (`reports/2025`: annual reports, proxy statements, annual letters), `presentations` (`presentations/2024`), `governance`, `esg` (`esg/2025`), `shareholder` (`shareholder/tax`, `shareholder/dividends`, `shareholder/stock`) and `other` (`other/faq`, `other/fact-sheets`, `other/financial-data[/2025]`, `other/web-pages`, `other/documents`). `…/undated` = no date could be read. `group` and `category` are null while a document has not been placed yet. A press release that is no call or event material is not a document: it is a news item, served by `GET /v1/news`.

### What you get

- Company-published material: displayed as published, not verified facts.

- `pages_url` is the per-page text (JSON). A link-only row (webcast) has `url` null and `link_status`.

- Files are served as permanent public URLs (immutable; a new version is a new URL), never proxied; they do not expire.

### Errors

- `503 media_unavailable` while the media base URL (`R2_PUBLIC_URL`) is not configured.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served; a foreign suffix (`SAP.DE`, `VOD.L`) or a crypto pair (`X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404.

### Changelog

- 2026-11: media URLs are permanent public URLs; `expires_at` removed.

get.description:
Search the page text of investor documents by keywords (default `mode=lexical`) or exact text (`literal`): the documents of earnings calls (CFO commentary, shareholder letters, data sheets, the company's own transcripts) and companies' IR libraries (annual reports, proxy statements, ESG reports, investor-day decks).

### What you get

- Up to 20 passages from company-published documents, with page numbers — not verified facts — and a permanent public URL of the file (open it at `#page=<page>`).

- Filter by company (`identifier`), kind, IR section, year or table.

- Each hit names the document's folder of the company's document tree (`group`, e.g. `earnings/fy2027/q2`, `group_label`, `category`), how it matched (`match`); the response says how much of the searched documents is indexed (`coverage`).

### Search modes

- `lexical` (default): keyword search — English full text with stemming; quoted phrases, `OR` and `-word` work; every word must match; ranked by `ts_rank_cd` (`websearch_to_tsquery`). Without `identifier`, at most 5,000 matching passages are ranked, split evenly between earnings-call documents and IR-library documents (each the first matches in index order, not the best) — add `identifier` to rank every match of one company. Finance tokens such as `FY2027`, `10-K`, `Q3` or `EBITDA` match as written.

- `literal`: the exact characters of the passage — no stemming, no fuzzy matching, `%` / `_` / `\` match themselves; case-sensitive unless `case_sensitive=false` (only allowed with `mode=literal`; default `true`). A pattern under 3 characters needs `identifier`. Newest first; `score` is 0.

- `match.spans` mark the matched characters in `text` (zero-based, end-exclusive Unicode code-point offsets); `text` is cut around the first match (`text_truncated`); `match.lexical_rank` is the hit's 1-based rank. Neither mode expands into fuzzy results. Both modes cost the same.

### Coverage

- `coverage.completeness` = `complete` (every searched passage is indexed: no hits is a genuine no-result), `partial` (some passages are still being indexed or failed) or `unknown` (nothing of the searched scope is indexed yet, or the counts could not be read) — read it before treating an empty list as "not found".

- `coverage.lexical` counts the searched transcripts or documents in the text index (`indexed`, `pending`, `failed`). `reasons` lists why the answer may be incomplete. The counts come from the indexing ledger: a transcript or document whose current version the index has not confirmed counts as `pending`; when they cannot be read, the hits are still returned with `completeness: unknown`, `lexical` null and `coverage_unavailable`.

### Changelog

- 2026-10: modes added and the default mode changed from semantic to `lexical`.

- 2026-11: modes `semantic` and `hybrid` removed; vector search is gone, pass `mode=lexical` (default) or `literal`.

- 2026-11: media URLs are permanent public URLs; `expires_at` removed.

### Errors

- `400` for a `mode=lexical` query of stopwords only (no searchable words), for `case_sensitive` with any mode but `literal`, and for a `mode=literal` pattern under 3 characters without a scope (see Search modes).

- `503 search_unavailable` (a search over its time limit — never an empty answer) carries `Retry-After`.

- `503 search_disabled` while search is switched off.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served; a foreign suffix (`SAP.DE`, `VOD.L`) or a crypto pair (`X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404.

Minimum tier for display: FREE.

The counts come from the indexing ledger: a transcript or document whose current version the index has not confirmed counts as `pending`; when they cannot be read, the hits are still returned with `completeness: unknown`, `lexical` null and `coverage_unavailable`.

get.description:
News of US companies — SEC filings and the companies' own newsroom publications — newest first.

### What you get

- Headline, lede (Invinite's), publication time, canonical URL, first source, kind, topics, the companies mentioned (`symbols`, `ciks`) and the companies' own publications of the item.

- Every item carries `attribution`; Invinite's summary of the publication is on `GET /v1/news/{id}` (`summary_words` = its length, null = the item has none: headline and link only).

### Filters

- `ticker` / `cik` = items mentioning the company (either matches); `publisher` = items the company published itself. Several filters intersect; several values of one filter match any of them.

- An unknown ticker is not an error: the list is empty.

### Pagination

- News is an append-heavy feed, so pages use a cursor instead of an offset: follow `next_url` (or pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same filters) until it is null. An item published between two calls never shifts a page — no duplicates, no gaps.

- Without `from` and `to`, the feed pages back through the whole history: the first page holds the newest entries, and `next_cursor` keeps going into older ones until there are none (null = the true end). Every other filter stays applied on every page.

- A feed without a company or item scope (`/v1/news` without `ticker` / `cik`, `/v1/news/developments` without `item_id`) reads one 92-day step per page: a page may then hold fewer entries than `limit`, or none, while `next_cursor` continues.

- With `from` and / or `to`, the window is at most 92 days and `next_cursor` stops at its edge; `next_url` pins the resolved `from` / `to`, so a default bound does not slide while you page.

### Sources and rights

- Items come from SEC EDGAR filings (`rights: public_record`) and the companies' own newsrooms (`rights: issuer`); wire services are never a source.

- Each development names the publication it was read from: `item` with its `attribution` (open `source_url` for the publisher's own words; `GET /v1/news/{id}` has Invinite's summary).

get.description:
Search the headlines, ledes and summaries of news items (SEC filings and the companies' own newsroom publications) by keywords (default `mode=lexical`) or exact text (`literal`). Ledes and summaries are Invinite's wording of the publication; the publisher's text is not searched.

### What you get

- Up to 8 passages, each with its news item (the `/v1/news` list item, incl. `attribution`), where it matched (`field`: `title`, `lede` or `summary`), the summary block it is from (`block`, see `/v1/news/{id}/text`) and how it matched (`match`); the response says how much of the searched news is indexed (`coverage`).

- Filter by `ticker` / `cik` (mentions, either matches), `publisher`, `publisher_host` (the host of the original URL), `kind`, `topic`, `field` and the publication window (`from` / `to`, default the last 365 days).

- A source whose owner reserved reuse keeps its headline searchable, never a lede or summary.

### Search modes

- `lexical` (default): keyword search — English full text with stemming; quoted phrases, `OR` and `-word` work; every word must match; ranked by `ts_rank_cd` (`websearch_to_tsquery`). Finance tokens such as `FY2027`, `10-K`, `Q3` or `EBITDA` match as written.

- `literal`: the exact characters of the passage — no stemming, no fuzzy matching, `%` / `_` / `\` match themselves; case-sensitive unless `case_sensitive=false` (only allowed with `mode=literal`; default `true`). A pattern under 3 characters needs `ticker`, `cik` or `publisher`. Newest first; `score` is 0.

- `match.spans` mark the matched characters in `text` (zero-based, end-exclusive Unicode code-point offsets); `text` is cut around the first match (`text_truncated`); `match.lexical_rank` is the hit's 1-based rank. Neither mode expands into fuzzy results. Both modes cost the same.

### Coverage

- `coverage.completeness` = `complete` (every searched passage is indexed: no hits is a genuine no-result), `partial` (some passages are still being indexed or failed) or `unknown` (nothing of the searched scope is indexed yet, or the counts could not be read) — read it before treating an empty list as "not found".

- `coverage.lexical` counts the searched transcripts or documents in the text index (`indexed`, `pending`, `failed`). `reasons` lists why the answer may be incomplete. The counts come from the indexing ledger: a transcript or document whose current version the index has not confirmed counts as `pending`; when they cannot be read, the hits are still returned with `completeness: unknown`, `lexical` null and `coverage_unavailable`.

### Changelog

- 2026-10: modes added and the default mode changed from semantic to `lexical`.

- 2026-11: modes `semantic` and `hybrid` removed; vector search is gone, pass `mode=lexical` (default) or `literal`.

### Errors

- `400` for a `mode=lexical` query of stopwords only (no searchable words), for `case_sensitive` with any mode but `literal`, and for a `mode=literal` pattern under 3 characters without a scope (see Search modes).

- `503 search_unavailable` (a search over its time limit — never an empty answer) carries `Retry-After`.

- `503 search_disabled` while search is switched off.

### Sources and rights

- Items come from SEC EDGAR filings (`rights: public_record`) and the companies' own newsrooms (`rights: issuer`); wire services are never a source.

- The text is Invinite's own summary of the publication (a complete rewording that keeps the facts); the publisher's text and media are never served. Wherever you show it, show `attribution.publisher`, `attribution.source_url` and `attribution.published_at` next to it (and the EDGAR form and accession for a filing). You may not resell it.

- A company that opted out, and a source whose owner reserved reuse, are not served (a reserved source keeps its headline, without text).

Minimum tier for display: FREE.

get.description:

Originals, figures and PDFs are permanent public URLs; nothing is fetched from SEC on request.

get.description:
Find passages in SEC documents, with citations: `mode=lexical` (default; keywords and quoted phrases, English stemming, ranked) or `mode=literal` (the exact characters; `case_sensitive=false` folds case). The earnings search contract: every hit carries `match` (`type`, `lexical_rank`, `spans` = code-point offsets into `text`), `document_spans` (offsets into the document text and each block), the cited blocks with neighbors and footnotes, and `citation` (version, block, the original's permanent URL). `coverage` says how complete the answer is: `forms_indexed` / `years_indexed` state the index policy; empty hits with `completeness: complete` is a genuine no-result, anything else is not. A search without a filer, entity or accession filter (no filter at all, or only `form` and / or `filed_from` / `filed_to`) reads at most `coverage.matches.cap` (300) matching passages of its forms and dates, newest filings first (`coverage.matches.order` `newest_first`: every match filed since `complete_since`, then older ones from `window_from` on): when more match, `readiness` is `partial` / `too_many_matches`, `coverage.matches` states how many passages were examined, that the total is unknown (`total: null`, `total_at_least`) and the filing dates the examined passages span, and `coverage.hint` says how to get complete results (add a filer, entity or accession filter; a narrower form or date range helps while it matches fewer than `cap`); the hits returned are still ranked and cited. A search with `cik`, `entity_id` or `accession` is never capped and gives complete results. The first search for a very common term after a backend restart can take about half a second longer (cold index pages). A capped search costs the same 100 credits (hits are returned). A stale or expired cursor answers 409 `restart_required`.

Read from Invinite's SEC document store: every answer carries `readiness` (`ready` / `partial` 200, `pending` 202 — retry later, not billed — `excluded` 403, `unknown` 404, `failed` 424, `not_ready` 503 while the capability is switched off). Originals, figures and PDFs are permanent public URLs; nothing is fetched from SEC on request.

Minimum tier for rag: STANDARD.

get.description: Ranked passages from SEC documents with citations (`mode=lexical` by default: keywords and quoted phrases, English stemming; `literal` for the exact characters). Each request reads one page of the index: `limit` above 50 answers 50 hits and a `next_cursor`; `match.lexical_rank` counts on across pages. `meta.index` says how complete the answer is: empty `data` with `completeness: complete` is a genuine no-result, anything else is not. A search without `company=` reads at most `meta.index.matches.cap` matching passages, newest filings first; `meta.index.hint` says how to narrow it.

ws.summary: WebSocket filings stream, live earnings-call transcripts and live news
ws.description:
One WebSocket connection streams new SEC filings as they are published, follows earnings calls live and pushes new news items. Authenticate with your API key. WebSocket sessions cost no credits (hence no `x-credits`).

### Filings

- New SEC filings arrive as `new_filing` frames. The connection needs the STANDARD plan.

- `filing` is the snake_case `WebSocketFiling`: the filing's index fields, `ticker` (null for a company that is not listed yet) and `proposed_symbols` (tickers an S-1 / F-1 registration statement proposes).

- Shape correction (2026-10): the frame used to forward the upstream camelCase envelope (`schemaVersion`, `eventKey`, `filing.accessionNumber`, …), not the documented object. It now sends exactly `WebSocketFiling`; a client that read the envelope must switch to the snake_case fields.

### Follow an earnings call live

Live transcripts use the channel `earnings-calls.live`, which requires the PRO plan.

1. Send a `subscribe` frame with an `event_id` or a `cik`. You receive `subscribed`.

2. `transcript_segment` frames arrive while the call is spoken, about 8 s after recognition (a quality hold), so the text trails the live audio: [Live audio and transcript sync](https://data.invinite.com/docs/live-sync); `speaker_names` snapshots name the speakers.

3. Lifecycle frames tell you where the call is: `call_started`, `call_ended`, `transcript_provisional`, `transcript_ready`, `rescheduled`.

4. The subscription ends with `unsubscribed` (its `reason` says why) after `transcript_ready` or `rescheduled`, 2 h after `call_ended` (the call produces nothing more), or 12 h after the scheduled start.

### Missed segments and reconnects

- Final segments arrive in `seq` order. A `gap` frame reports a range that did not arrive within 1.5 s; a late final may still follow.

- After a reconnect, subscribe again with `since_seq` set to the last final `seq` you hold: the missed finals are replayed, then live delivery continues. `resume_unavailable` means the call cannot be replayed.

- An `error` frame with code `unavailable` reports a server-side failure. The connection always stays open.

### Keyword alerts

- Add `keywords` (up to 20) to a subscription and every final segment that contains one also sends a `keyword_hit` frame. `keyword_match` is `exact` or `stem`; `speaker_roles` keeps, for example, management's words only.

- A hit carries the speaker's provisional name and role, the previous final segment as context, and `latency_ms`: the relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time, so it includes the release hold of about 8 s (your network is not included).

### Guidance flashes

- Every subscription to a call receives `guidance_flash` frames: forward-looking numbers, extracted after the transcript's release hold of about 8 s.

### All live calls in one subscription

- `scope: all_live` with `keywords` (and no `event_id` or `cik`) follows every call being captured live for one subscription slot. It receives keyword hits only, never segments. `min_rank` limits the companies; `events` can add `guidance_flash`.

- A `warning` frame (`global_scope_degraded`) says a new call was not attached.

- At `transcript_ready` it also receives the final transcript's hits once (`layer: final`), without those a live hit already covered within ± 5 s.

### Live prices

- `prices: true` on a per-call subscription adds `price_tick` frames (at most one per second): that second's OHLC and volume, the return in bp since the last trade before the call started and since the previous close, and `call_ms` on the transcript clock.

- A tick shows what happened at the same time, not what caused it. Pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse.

- `prices` with `scope: all_live` is refused (`bad_message`). `GET /v1/earnings-calls/live` says `live_prices: true` while ticks flow.

### Live news

Live news uses the channel `news.live`, which requires the STANDARD plan.

1. Send `subscribe` with `channel: news.live` and optional filters: `tickers`, `ciks` (either matches), `earnings_only`, `kinds`, `sources` (`edgar`, `ir`). No filter = every item. You receive `subscribed` with the normalised filters; a second `subscribe` replaces them.

2. Every new item arrives once as a `news_item` frame: the same object as a `GET /v1/news` row, with its `attribution` (publisher, original URL, date, rights) — show it with the text.

3. `unsubscribe` with `channel: news.live` stops it (`unsubscribed`). `error` frames of the channel carry `channel: news.live`; `channel_unavailable` means live news is switched off.

- Push covers new items only: corrections (a new revision), later enrichment (developments) and items without a ticker are not pushed, and an item missed during a disconnect is not replayed — `GET /v1/news` (with `from`) has every item.

Minimum tier for display: FREE.

post.description: A new news item (an SEC filing or a company's own publication), the same object as a GET /v1/news row with its attribution. Fired once per item when the pipeline announces it — corrections, later enrichment and items without a ticker are not pushed (read GET /v1/news). filters.ciks matches any CIK the item mentions; filters.keywords (PRO) narrow to items whose headline or lede names one

data.description: A new news item (an SEC filing or a company's own publication), the same object as a GET /v1/news row with its attribution. Fired once per item when the pipeline announces it — corrections, later enrichment and items without a ticker are not pushed (read GET /v1/news). filters.ciks matches any CIK the item mentions; filters.keywords (PRO) narrow to items whose headline or lede names one

id.description: Stable item id (a correction is a new item, see supersedes_id)

description.description: Lede: one or two sentences written by Invinite with the summary (never the publisher's words); null for an item without a summary (title-only, metadata-only) or whose publisher reserved reuse

url.description: Canonical URL of the item (the first publication)

id.description: `edgar` or `ir` (a company newsroom)

host.description: The newsroom host of an `ir` source; null otherwise

topics.description: Development topics found in the text

rights.description: public_record = an SEC filing; issuer = the company's own publication

is_earnings_news.description: Results, results date, call announcement or guidance

earnings.description: The fiscal period an earnings item belongs to; null when none was found

conference_date.description: The results call it announces or follows

revision.description: Revision of the publication (grows when the publisher corrects it)

supersedes_id.description: The older item this one corrects

url.description: The company's own publication

published_at.description: Publication time the newsroom states (else when we first saw it)

id.description: The newsroom's own id of the label, when it has one

label.description: The label as the newsroom shows it

url.description: The newsroom's page of the label

id.description: The newsroom's own id of the label, when it has one

label.description: The label as the newsroom shows it

url.description: The newsroom's page of the label

tags.description: The newsroom's own tags

publications.description: The companies' own verified publications of the item, oldest first (at most 10)

publications_truncated.description: More than 10 publications exist (the detail lists every sighting)

model_processing_allowed.description: false = the publisher reserved text and data mining of its original publication (a machine-readable reservation read at fetch time). Informational: every text this API serves — lede, summary, developments — is Invinite's own wording; the headline is the publisher's

summary_words.description: Words of the item's summary (`GET /v1/news/{id}` serves it); null for an item without one (title-only, metadata-only or a reserved source)

attribution.description: Who published what the text summarises, where and when (show publisher, source URL and date wherever you show the text)

publisher.description: Publisher of the summarised publication: the company, or SEC EDGAR for a filing

source_url.description: The original publication the summary was written from

rights.description: public_record = an SEC filing; issuer = the company's own publication

edgar.description: The filing of an SEC item; null otherwise

enum: Summary written by Invinite from the publication above; not the publisher's text. Source and date above.
statement.description: The attribution sentence to carry with the text

has_pdf.description: Whether a PDF exists at delivery. The PDF renders after publication, so false usually means not yet: read `pdf` from the REST route later; no webhook carries its URL

post.description: A test delivery, or the notice that the subscription was disabled

data.description: A test delivery, or the notice that the subscription was disabled
